title: Atlas Core controlled execution outbox security assessment
scope: Post-approval execution queue, provider executor registry, idempotency, outcome reconciliation, rollback receipts, official SDK, Gateway permissions, and sandbox-limited operator controls

approved_targets: Disposable SQLite databases and synthetic action executors
Loopback operator and Gateway test services
prohibited_actions: Register a live vendor executor or credential
Send an action to a real company system
Change production identity, permissions, firewall, or TLS
Represent a synthetic receipt as a real business outcome

trust_boundaries: Execution queue to server-registered provider adapter
Provider outcome to minimized durable receipt
Ambiguous provider outcome to privileged reconciliation
Execution receipt to SDK, Gateway, and read-only operator
data_flows: Approved proposal to confirmation-guarded durable queue
Proposal payload and stable idempotency key to allowlisted executor
Bounded operator-safe outcome summary to Company Memory
Uncertain outcome to explicit reconciliation without automatic retry
Succeeded outcome to separately confirmed rollback adapter

threats.name: Action executes without human approval
threats.control: Queue transaction requires the proposal to be human-approved and an exact proposal/executor confirmation

threats.name: Duplicate provider mutation
threats.control: One execution per proposal, stable unique idempotency key, transactional claim, terminal replay receipts, and maximum three definite-failure attempts

threats.name: Ambiguous network failure is retried and duplicates work
threats.control: Executor exceptions become uncertain; Atlas refuses retry until a separately confirmed reconciliation records a definite outcome

threats.name: Caller selects an arbitrary endpoint or action
threats.control: Executors are server-registered objects with validated identifiers and explicit action-type allowlists; request URLs and credentials are not accepted by queue APIs

threats.name: Remote caller self-asserts audit identity
threats.control: Gateway binds queue and reconciliation actor fields to the authenticated grant name and uses separate execute and reconcile permissions

threats.name: Receipt or UI leaks action payload or provider secrets
threats.control: Execution receipts and audit events omit proposal payload; result text and references are bounded and executor authors must supply operator-safe summaries

threats.name: Rollback is treated as automatic or guaranteed
threats.control: Rollback requires a definitely succeeded action, exact separate confirmation, registered support, and its own succeeded or failed receipt

findings.finding: A live executor must implement provider-specific idempotency and safe outcome parsing. Atlas supplies the stable key but cannot prove a vendor honors it until that adapter and provider are tested.

Abrupt process termination while an action is running leaves a running receipt whose external outcome is unknown. Atlas does not auto-reclaim or retry it; an operational reconciliation procedure is required.
The localhost operator can queue, run, and roll back only the built-in Hotel/PMS sandbox. It refuses receipts for every other executor and does not expose reconciliation.

validation: Ninety-one full-suite tests passed on Python 3.12
Python compileall and operator JavaScript syntax passed
Fresh core, SDK, Gateway, and Operator wheels installed and passed the Hotel/PMS sandbox execution smoke through the authenticated remote SDK
Live localhost Hotel workspace completed approval, execution, provider-state verification, and rollback with no console errors or desktop horizontal overflow
residual_risk: No live provider executor, credential, sandbox account, or real action has been authorized or tested.
Provider-specific idempotency, rollback semantics, rate limits, audit fields, and incident procedures require adapter-level review.
Crash recovery for a running execution is intentionally manual because silent retry could duplicate an external mutation.
This assessment is implementation evidence and not a compliance certification.
